chords._schema: strings ordered low E (6) to high e (1). frets: null = muted/not played, 0 = open. fingers: 0 = open, 1 = index, 2 = middle, 3 = ring, 4 = pinky, null = muted.

easyC.name: C major (Lauren's 'easy C' — 2-finger reduction)
easyC.note: Reduced 2-finger C voicing for confidence-building. Spelling verified deterministically by chord-theory-check.js (2026-08-08) as C E G. 'Lauren's easy C' is a teaching label; arithmetic proves the fingering spells C major and is playable.

pivot_points.static_finger: middle(2) stays on D-string 2nd fret in both Em and standard C
pivot_points.movement: ring(3) A2->A3; index(1) added on B 1st (standard C).

pivot_points.static_finger: index(1) lands on A-string 2nd fret in G
pivot_points.movement: ring(3) D2->high-e 3rd; middle(2) added on low-E 3rd.

exercises.name: Spider exercise

params.breathing_cue: breathe; do not hold breath (tension = slow)

exercises.coaching: Spider: start at the 7th fret where it is least stretchy. One finger per fret — index, middle, ring. Three slow picks per string, top to bottom and back. Floppy fingers are normal; that is the control you are building.

exercises.name: Finger lift-off

params.action: lift 3rd, then 2nd, then 1st, one at a time; rebuild
params.air_variant: lift hand off, make shapes in air, drop back down

exercises.coaching: Make a C shape and lift fingers one at a time. If your hand forgets the shape when you let go, that is expected — reps fix it. We are teaching your fingers where to go.

exercises.name: 1-minute change drill

params.push_technique: set tempo slightly above comfort, then return
params.clarity_rule: during speed push, muted strings OK; goal is finger SPEED

exercises.coaching: Metronome on, Em to easy C for one minute. Count your changes. Do not worry about buzz — we are chasing speed. Write the number down; next week, beat it.

avatar_coaching_copy.intro: Slow chord changes are not a talent problem — they are a muscle-memory problem. Today we warm up your hands and turn the metronome into a scorecard.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex1_intro: Spider: 7th fret, least stretch. Index, middle, ring, one per fret. Three slow picks per string, up and down. Breathe — floppy fingers are the control forming.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex2_intro: Make a C, lift fingers one at a time. Hand flattens when you let go? Normal. Muscle memory has not formed yet. Reps fix it.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex3_intro: Scorecard time: Em to easy C, one minute, count the changes. Speed first, clean second. Write it down — that number is next week's target.
avatar_coaching_copy.results: Your count this session is your baseline. Next session, beat it by one. That is how 16 becomes 30.
avatar_coaching_copy.wrap: Consistency beats talent. Three drills, five minutes, most days — that is the whole secret to fast changes.

lesson.title: Faster Chord Changes (SPEED BUILDER)
lesson.one_line_promise: Turn "I can change" into "I can change fast."
objectives: Warm up hands with the spider exercise
Build finger independence with lift-off drills
Use a metronome as a scorecard for change speed
Use pivot points to make Em-C and Em-G easier
prerequisites: Em, C, G, D open chords (even slowly)

free_metronome: EX3 uses built-in metronome — funnel front door
adaptive_loop: raise target changes/min week over week
